name: Nucleofill
lead: Nucleofill is a range of injectable polynucleotide (PN) skin boosters made by the Italian company Promoitalia. Clinics offer it as an aesthetic procedure to improve skin quality: hydration, firmness, fine lines and the look of scars on the face, neck, hands and other areas.[1]

The best-known product, Nucleofill Strong, contains polymerised polynucleotide at 25 mg/ml (2.5 percent) in a prefilled 1.5 ml syringe and is delivered by a practitioner through intradermal micro-injections, usually as a short series of sessions followed by maintenance.[1] Other versions in the range target the eye area and other uses.

Seller pages describe the effects as lasting around 6 to 9 months. [1] Polynucleotides as a class have been reviewed in the aesthetic literature: a 2024 systematic review of nine studies with 219 patients reported improvements in wrinkles, skin texture and elasticity with mild, temporary side effects. [2] No peer-reviewed trials of the Nucleofill brand were found.

chain: Polynucleotide gel injected into the dermis
angle.text: Nucleofill is injected by clinicians into the skin of the face, neck and hands to improve hydration, firmness and fine lines. People choose it as a skin-quality treatment rather than a volume filler.

paras: Nucleofill Strong is sold as a sterile prefilled syringe of polymerised polynucleotide, described as derived from natural sources, with a mix of vitamins, amino acids, coenzymes and minerals.[1] The seller restricts sales to licensed professionals.[1]

Seller materials describe firming and tightening, hydration, reduced fine lines, protection against oxidative stress, stimulation of collagen and elastin, and a lessened look of scars and stretch marks.[1]

Wikipedia notes that fish-derived polynucleotide is used in aesthetic medicine as a dermal filler. [3] Polynucleotide injections are positioned as skin-quality treatments that improve hydration, elasticity and texture rather than adding volume. [2]

The seller lists mild redness, swelling, bruising, tenderness or itching at injection sites, usually resolving within a few days. Listed contraindications include known allergy to polynucleotides, active skin infection or inflammation at the site, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and autoimmune disorders or compromised immunity.[1]

No studies found on Nucleofill products specifically. Studies of polynucleotides as a category exist: a 2024 systematic review in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology (Lampridou, Bassett, Cavallini and Christopoulos) included nine studies of low to moderate quality covering 219 patients. It reported promising results for wrinkles, texture and elasticity, statistically significant in several studies, mostly mild and temporary side effects, and moderate to high patient satisfaction, while noting limited consensus on optimal use and calling for higher-quality trials. [2]

card.summary: Promoitalia's injectable polynucleotide skin booster, used by clinics to improve hydration, firmness and fine lines.
card.note: Professional injectable; seller-reported contraindications include pregnancy and autoimmune disorders.

quick.overview:
Nucleofill is a brand of polynucleotide gels injected into the skin by clinicians. People get it to improve skin hydration, texture and fine lines on the face, neck and hands.

A typical course is a few sessions several weeks apart with maintenance later; sellers describe results lasting several months.
quick.mechanism: Polynucleotides are delivered into the dermis by micro-injection; sellers claim they hydrate the skin and stimulate collagen and elastin.
quick.risks: Reported side effects are mild injection-site redness, swelling, bruising and itching. Sellers list pregnancy, infection at the site and autoimmune conditions as contraindications.
